blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: GVA at Basic Prices includes production taxes and excludes product subsidies, serving as the bridge between producer factor costs and consumer market prices under SNA 2008.

blocks.content: 🗺️ Valuation Spectrum: Factor Cost → Basic Prices → Market Price
1. Factor Cost ($FC$): Pure cost of production factors (Rent + Wages + Interest + Profit). Excludes all taxes and subsidies.
2. Basic Prices ($BP$): $BP = FC + \text{Production Taxes} - \text{Production Subsidies}$. Includes taxes independent of output volume (Land Revenue, Stamp Duty, Registration Fee).
3. Market Price ($MP$): $MP = BP + \text{Product Taxes} - \text{Product Subsidies}$. Includes volume-dependent taxes (GST, Excise, Customs Duty).
4. Headline Growth Measure: In 2015, NSO adopted **GVA at Basic Prices** for sectoral growth and **GDP at Market Price** as headline GDP, aligning with UN SNA 2008.

rows: Paid irrespective of actual volume of production
Land Revenue, Stamp Duty, Registration Fees, Factory License Fees
Received irrespective of actual volume of production
Subsidies to Small Scale Industries, Farmers' Land Subsidies
Paid per unit of product produced / sold
Goods and Services Tax (GST), Excise Duty, Customs Duty, Sales Tax
Granted per unit of product produced / sold
Food Subsidy (TPDS), Fertilizer Subsidy, LPG Subsidy

blocks.content: $$\mathbf{GVA \text{ at Basic Prices} = GVA \text{ at Factor Cost} + \text{Production Taxes} - \text{Production Subsidies}}$$
$$\mathbf{GDP \text{ at Market Price} = GVA \text{ at Basic Prices} + \text{Product Taxes} - \text{Product Subsidies}}$$
Prior to 2015, India reported headline GDP growth at **GDP at Factor Cost**. In 2015, CSO/NSO made 3 major changes:

items: Headline economic growth switched to **GDP at Market Price** (matching global practice).
Sectoral performance switched to **GVA at Basic Prices**.
Replaced manufacturing census data with **MCA-21 database** (Ministry of Corporate Affairs online filings) for corporate sector income estimation.

blocks.content: ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** GST is a **Product Tax** (volume dependent), whereas Stamp Duty on factory land is a **Production Tax** (volume independent).
⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** If Product Subsidies exceed Product Taxes in a crisis year, $GDP_{MP}$ will be **LESS** than $GVA 	ext{ at Basic Prices}$!

#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which of the following is classified as a 'Production Tax' (independent of actual production volume) under NSO national accounting rules?  
(A) Goods and Services Tax (GST)  
(B) Customs Duty  
(C) Land Revenue & Stamp Duty  
(D) Central Excise Duty  
**Answer: — Land Revenue and Stamp Duty are paid irrespective of production volume.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** A manufacturing sector has GVA at Factor Cost $= ₹500	ext{ Cr}$. Production Taxes $= ₹30	ext{ Cr}$, Production Subsidies $= ₹10	ext{ Cr}$, Product Taxes $= ₹80	ext{ Cr}$, and Product Subsidies $= ₹40	ext{ Cr}$. Calculate GVA at Basic Prices and GDP at Market Price.  
**Resolution:**

items: $	ext{GVA at Basic Prices} = 500 + 30 - 10 = mathbf{₹520	ext{ Cr}}$.
$	ext{GDP at Market Price} = 520 + 80 - 40 = mathbf{₹560	ext{ Cr}}$.

blocks.content:
#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Explain the distinction between Factor Cost, Basic Prices, and Market Price. Why did India adopt GVA at Basic Prices and MCA-21 database in the 2015 NSO base year revision?'*

🎯 Exam Angle → 🔥 HIGH — National Income Invariant: National Income in India is officially defined as **NNP at Factor Cost** ((	ext{NNP}_{	ext{FC}})). Formula: (	ext{GVA}_{	ext{Basic Prices}} = 	ext{GDP}_{	ext{MP}} - 	ext{Product Taxes} + 	ext{Product Subsidies}).
